headline: Ten Plays, Five Wins, And Fifty Six Cents Of Glory
paragraphs: Ten games graded for real, four waved off, six deemed worthy of action, and ten plays fired at ten dollars apiece. The ledger came back 5-5 for a profit of 0.56, an ROI of 0.6 percent. That is a week of work, a hundred dollars at risk, and a return that would not cover the tip on a coffee. The model expected 59.6 percent and hit 50.0.

The Washington trip to Purdue was the whole show. Spread, total and moneyline all cashed off a 38-26 final, with the plus 142 moneyline returning 14.20 and the Over 50.5 landing as the best call of the week at 9.09. Then Texas State 66, Colorado State 27 happened, and the model, 66 percent sure of an Under 70.5, watched the teams clear that number with a quarter to spare. The Colorado State plus 14.5 died in the same wreckage.

Totals finished 2-1 for 8.18 and moneylines 1-1 for 4.20, while spreads went 2-3 and gave back 11.82. Nine plays saw their line move and exactly zero of those moves went toward the model, which is 0.0 percent, a figure you have to work at. Season now reads 98-108-4 across 210 plays, down 111.78, ROI negative 5.3, with expected 60.3 against an actual 47.6. The one hindsight graded week sits there at 40-25-1 and plus 110.47, scored after the fact, worth precisely nothing.
